newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint firms v basket as shrugs off Czech troubles.
newsitem.headline: Forint firms v basket as shrugs off Czech troubles.

text.p: The Hungarian forint closed firmer against both the central bank's currency basket and the dollar on Thursday as nervousness of a spillover from the Czech crown's fall evaporated, dealers said.
The forint finished the day at 182.40/45 to the dollar, compared to 182.45/50 in the morning and 182.50/54 at midday.
The Hungarian currency narrowed its gap from the central bank's resistance level (NBH bid) to around 20 fillers by the end of the session from about 40 at the start of trade.
"I would say the nervousness from the Czech crown's fall has passed and things are back to normal," said Istvan Gere of ING Bank.
Some dealers had discerned signs early on the day that some foreign investors were withdrawing from the forex market. However, Gere said the trend did not materialise.
"I don't see anyone pulling out of the market now," he said.
The forint floats within the central bank's 4.5 percent wide intervention range, against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
